learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Exploration progress is not mastery evidence; quiz attempts remain the scored retrieval signal.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: The group maintains desired capacity within configured __________.

reveal.text: The group maintains desired capacity within configured minimum and maximum bounds.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Scale out adds capacity; scale __________.

reveal.text: Scale out adds capacity; scale in removes capacity.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Maintain N healthy instances and replace failed ones” → __________

reveal.text: EC2 Auto Scaling. It maintains desired capacity and can replace unhealthy instances.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A launch template captures reusable EC2 launch settings such as AMI __________.

reveal.text: A launch template captures reusable EC2 launch settings such as AMI, instance type, networking, and storage.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Point the Auto Scaling configuration at the intended launch template version __________.

reveal.text: Point the Auto Scaling configuration at the intended launch template version and roll out safely.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It describes how __________.

reveal.text: It describes how to launch instances; scaling policies decide when capacity changes.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Target tracking automatically adjusts capacity to keep a selected metric __________.

reveal.text: Target tracking automatically adjusts capacity to keep a selected metric near the configured target.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Keep average CPU around 50%” → __________

reveal.text: Target tracking scaling policy. It adjusts capacity to keep a target metric near the configured value.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It reacts to metric behavior continuously rather than running only __________.

reveal.text: It reacts to metric behavior continuously rather than running only at a fixed time.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Step scaling applies different adjustments depending on how far __________.

reveal.text: Step scaling applies different adjustments depending on how far a metric breaches thresholds.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Good when moderate and severe load should __________.

reveal.text: Good when moderate and severe load should trigger different scaling adjustments.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Step scaling: threshold bands and explicit adjustments | Target tracking: __________

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Scheduled: known time-based capacity change | Predictive: __________

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Scheduled scaling fits a __________.

reveal.text: Scheduled scaling fits a known recurring time.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Predictive scaling can prepare capacity based __________.

reveal.text: Predictive scaling can prepare capacity based on forecast demand.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Warmup prevents new-instance metrics from distorting __________.

reveal.text: Warmup prevents new-instance metrics from distorting some scaling behavior; the health check grace period gives new instances time before health evaluation can replace them.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “New instances are replaced before app startup finishes” → check __________.

reveal.text: Health check grace period, startup timing, and load balancer health checks. Verify the app has enough time to become healthy.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It only delays __________.

reveal.text: It only delays health evaluation; fix the actual startup/health problem too.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Scale worker capacity with backlog or backlog-per-instance metrics when work __________.

reveal.text: Scale worker capacity with backlog or backlog-per-instance metrics when work arrives through a queue.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Normalize demand by active capacity so the metric represents __________.

reveal.text: Normalize demand by active capacity so the metric represents work pressure per worker.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Messages pile up faster than EC2 workers process them” → __________

reveal.text: Queue/backlog-driven Auto Scaling. Scale workers using a queue-related metric when backlog grows.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: CloudFront serves cached content from edge locations when __________.

reveal.text: CloudFront serves cached content from edge locations when requests match cached objects.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A cache miss or expired object causes CloudFront to __________.

reveal.text: A cache miss or expired object causes CloudFront to fetch from the origin.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Global users, static/dynamic HTTP content, reduce origin load” → __________

reveal.text: Amazon CloudFront. It serves content through edge locations and can reduce origin load.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Separate what varies the cache from what must merely be __________.

reveal.text: Separate what varies the cache from what must merely be forwarded to the origin.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Unnecessary headers/cookies/query strings in the cache __________.

reveal.text: Unnecessary headers/cookies/query strings in the cache key fragment the cache.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Use an origin request policy when the origin needs a value __________.

reveal.text: Use an origin request policy when the origin needs a value but cached variants do not.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: ElastiCache can offload reads/session/cache workloads __________.

reveal.text: ElastiCache can offload reads/session/cache workloads from slower backends.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Best when the application can tolerate cache semantics and benefits __________.

reveal.text: Best when the application can tolerate cache semantics and benefits from low-latency repeated access.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Most architectures keep __________.

reveal.text: Most architectures keep durable state elsewhere.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Valkey/Redis OSS: richer data structures, replication/HA features | Memcached: __________

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Valkey/Redis OSS family is usually __________.

reveal.text: Valkey/Redis OSS family is usually the stronger clue.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Memcached is a common fit for __________.

reveal.text: Memcached is a common fit for a simple distributed cache.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Use storage autoscaling for storage growth, instance-class changes for compute/memory, and read replicas __________.

reveal.text: Use storage autoscaling for storage growth, instance-class changes for compute/memory, and read replicas for read scaling where supported.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Read replica: read scaling; can have DR uses | Multi-AZ: __________

columns.title: Read replica
items: read scaling; can have DR uses

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Read-heavy database, writes are fine” → __________

reveal.text: Read replicas or engine-specific read scaling. Use them when reads are the bottleneck and writes are acceptable.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Aurora Auto Scaling can add/remove Aurora Replicas based on __________.

reveal.text: Aurora Auto Scaling can add/remove Aurora Replicas based on configured metrics and limits.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Scale read capacity by adjusting replicas __________.

reveal.text: Scale read capacity by adjusting replicas in supported Aurora clusters.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Replica count scaling is different from __________.

reveal.text: Replica count scaling is different from changing DB instance classes.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: On-demand: capacity managed per request volume | Provisioned: __________

columns.title: Provisioned
items: set capacity; optionally use auto scaling

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: On-demand capacity is often simpler __________.

reveal.text: On-demand capacity is often simpler for unpredictable traffic.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling __________.

reveal.text: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling can be appropriate.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: ALB: HTTP/HTTPS, Layer 7 routing | NLB: __________ | GWLB: __________

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Path/host routing → __________; static IP/L4 → __________.

reveal.text: ALB for path/host-based Layer 7 routing; NLB for high-performance Layer 4 traffic and static IP needs.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Protocol, routing features, target type, performance, and network-appliance __________.

reveal.text: Protocol, routing features, target type, performance, and network-appliance needs drive the choice.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: The load balancer routes to targets __________.

reveal.text: The load balancer routes to targets in target groups; health checks determine which targets are eligible.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Check success codes/timeouts/thresholds __________.

reveal.text: Check success codes/timeouts/thresholds plus network reachability.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: ELB: target health inside load-balancing path | Route 53: __________

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Cross-zone behavior controls how load balancer nodes distribute traffic __________.

reveal.text: Cross-zone behavior controls how load balancer nodes distribute traffic across enabled Availability Zones/targets.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: It gives existing connections/requests time to complete while __________.

reveal.text: It gives existing connections/requests time to complete while a target is draining.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Deploy/remove instances without dropping active requests” → __________

reveal.text: Deregistration delay plus healthy rolling behavior. Let in-flight requests drain before removing targets.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Route 53 can use health information with routing policies __________.

reveal.text: Route 53 can use health information with routing policies to influence DNS answers.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Failover routing supports primary __________.

reveal.text: Failover routing supports primary and secondary records.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: It can use supported AWS target health rather than a __________.

reveal.text: It can use supported AWS target health rather than a separate endpoint health check.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Multi-AZ deployments improve availability by maintaining redundant database __________.

reveal.text: Multi-AZ deployments improve availability by maintaining redundant database capacity and supporting failover.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Multi-AZ: availability/failover | Read replica: __________

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Automatic failover during AZ/DB failure” → __________

reveal.text: RDS Multi-AZ. It is designed for availability and automatic failover rather than read scaling.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: For supported Valkey/Redis OSS configurations, Multi-AZ can automatically fail __________.

reveal.text: For supported Valkey/Redis OSS configurations, Multi-AZ can automatically fail over to a replica.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Its architecture differs from Valkey/Redis OSS __________.

reveal.text: Its architecture differs from Valkey/Redis OSS replication and Multi-AZ failover.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Cache must survive node/AZ failure with failover” → __________

reveal.text: Replicated Valkey/Redis OSS with Multi-AZ where supported. Use it when cache availability and failover matter.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Choose regional/Multi-AZ options where supported when the workload must tolerate __________.

reveal.text: Choose regional/Multi-AZ options where supported when the workload must tolerate infrastructure or AZ failure.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Protocol, OS integration, performance, features, and __________.

reveal.text: Protocol, OS integration, performance, features, and availability model differ.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: SMB + Windows ACLs + managed HA → consider __________.

reveal.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. It is a strong fit for SMB, Windows ACLs, and managed Windows file storage.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Distribute capacity across Availability Zones, route only to healthy targets __________.

reveal.text: Distribute capacity across Availability Zones, route only to healthy targets, and replace/scale instances automatically.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: HA is end-to-end; a redundant frontend cannot compensate for a single __________.

reveal.text: HA is end-to-end; a redundant frontend cannot compensate for a single point of failure elsewhere.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Stay available if an AZ fails” → design across __________.

reveal.text: Multiple Availability Zones. Design each critical tier so an AZ failure does not create a single point of failure.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Recovery points are stored in backup vaults according to __________.

reveal.text: Recovery points are stored in backup vaults according to plan rules and policies.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Backup centralizes scheduling, retention, and __________.

reveal.text: AWS Backup centralizes scheduling, retention, and governance for supported services.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: A backup strategy should __________.

reveal.text: A backup strategy should include restore validation/testing.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Where supported, backup copies support additional isolation and recovery locations such __________.

reveal.text: Where supported, backup copies support additional isolation and recovery locations such as another Region or account.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Restore testing verifies that selected backups __________.

reveal.text: Restore testing verifies that selected backups can actually be restored.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Compliance requires evidence backups can be restored” → __________

reveal.text: AWS Backup restore testing. It provides evidence that selected backups can actually be restored.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: An AMI references the information needed to launch an EC2 instance __________.

reveal.text: An AMI references the information needed to launch an EC2 instance, including block-device snapshot mappings.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Create/manage an AMI rather than only __________.

reveal.text: Create/manage an AMI rather than only an individual volume snapshot.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Coordinate the application/filesystem when consistency __________.

reveal.text: Coordinate the application/filesystem when consistency across writes matters.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Automated backup: retention window; supports point-in-time recovery | Manual snapshot: __________

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Point-in-time restore uses automated backups and transaction logs within __________.

reveal.text: Point-in-time restore uses automated backups and transaction logs within the supported retention period.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Restore to just before accidental change” → __________

reveal.text: Point-in-time recovery (PITR). Restore the database to a time just before the unwanted change.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: On-demand backup: manual snapshot-like recovery point | PITR: __________

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time __________.

reveal.text: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: DynamoDB restore workflows create a new table rather than rewinding the __________.

reveal.text: DynamoDB restore workflows create a new table rather than rewinding the live table in place.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Versioning preserves object versions so accidental overwrite/delete __________.

reveal.text: Versioning preserves object versions so accidental overwrite/delete scenarios can be recovered.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: A delete marker becomes the current version while __________.

reveal.text: A delete marker becomes the current version while older versions remain recoverable.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Replication copies objects/versions __________.

reveal.text: Replication copies objects/versions to another destination; versioning preserves versions in a bucket.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: S3 replication can copy eligible objects to a configured __________.

reveal.text: S3 replication can copy eligible objects to a configured destination, including cross-Region patterns.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Replication provides an additional copy according to __________.

reveal.text: Replication provides an additional copy according to replication rules and requirements.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Existing-object replication/backfill requires a supported mechanism rather than assuming the live __________.

reveal.text: Existing-object replication/backfill requires a supported mechanism rather than assuming the live rule covers all history.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: FSx backup protects __________.

reveal.text: FSx backup protects the file system; FSx for Windows shadow copies can provide point-in-time file/folder recovery.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Shadow copies are a common __________.

reveal.text: Shadow copies are a common fit if configured.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Use backups/replication according to recovery __________.

reveal.text: Use backups/replication according to recovery and retention requirements.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: RTO is the target time __________.

reveal.text: RTO is the target time to restore service; RPO is the maximum acceptable data-loss window.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Stricter recovery objectives generally require more replication __________.

reveal.text: Stricter recovery objectives generally require more replication, automation, and pre-provisioned resources.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “No more than 15 minutes of data loss” → __________.

reveal.text: RPO requirement. It defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Backup & restore → Pilot light → __________ → Active/active

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Pilot light: critical core running; scale rest after disaster | Warm standby: __________

columns.title: Pilot light
items: critical core running; scale rest after disaster

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Near-zero recovery with traffic served from multiple sites” → __________.

reveal.text: Active/active multi-site. It provides the fastest recovery profile among the standard DR patterns.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Lowest steady-state cost; slower recovery acceptable” → __________.

reveal.text: Backup and restore. It usually has the lowest steady-state cost but the slowest recovery.

authoring_notes: Original learning content. Official SOA-C03 exam guide revision 1.1 is the scope authority; the supplied May 2026 study guide was used as a supplementary coverage check and was not copied. Prompt placeholders were revised in v2 so ordinary prompts directly cloze or structurally preview the revealed content. Exam-clue prompts retain certification-style scenario wording and now reveal a direct answer first.
